Only idp-alias-1 is removed, by the test itself at line 428, so 20 of the 21 leak rather than all 21.

findings.claim: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate evaluates the login predicate on the org-aware wrapped original from getById() but on the raw unwrapped updated model. While the linked organization is disabled, both can fail the predicate and the method returns early, so the ORG_ONLY/ALL login caches are not invalidated. After the organization is re-enabled, stale entries surface hidden, link-only or non-public IdPs.

verifier.reason: `update()` passes the org-aware wrapper from `getById()` as `original` (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:91-93, wrapper `isEnabled()` at :436-441) and the raw model as `updated`, so with the org disabled, hiding/link-only/un-publicing an IdP fails the predicate on both sides and returns early at :405-407. Org enable/disable never invalidates the login keys (InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:300-308), and after re-enable the bean only re-checks `isEnabled()` (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:75,80), so the stale cached id is shown.

findings.claim: LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate(), a public SPI predicate, now includes 'organizationId == null || BROKER_PUBLIC'. Because of this, organization-linked non-public IdPs are hidden outside the cache, e.g. in IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate() when the Organization feature is off, where they were previously shown.

verifier.reason: The patch adds `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC` to the shared `getLoginPredicate()` (server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254), which `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` returns unchanged (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/IdentityProviderBean.java:226). With the Organization feature off the plain bean is used (FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:482-486) and models still carry the stored organizationId (JpaIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:539), so an org-linked non-public IdP among a user's federated identities is now filtered out where it previously passed.

findings.claim: ORG_ONLY/ALL login results for all organizations are stored in one IdentityProviderListQuery per realm and mode. Each new org miss bumps the revision and copies the whole previous map, so the entry grows unbounded. Concurrent misses for different orgs defeat addRevisioned, and any login-IdP change drops the results for every org.

verifier.reason: The login cache key is only realm+mode (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:215) with the org id as an inner map key (:223); an org miss calls invalidateObject, which removes the entry and bumps the revision (:236, CacheManager.java:124-132), then rebuilds via putAll of the previous map (IdentityProviderListQuery.java:43) with no eviction, so it grows with the number of orgs queried. A concurrent miss for another org either makes addRevisioned skip the put (CacheManager.java:175) or overwrites from a stale `query`, and registerIDPLoginInvalidation invalidates every mode's key, dropping all orgs (InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:382-388).

findings.claim: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), so the lookup re-enters the same caching layer.

verifier.reason: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:246 does call session.identityProviders().getById(id) inside getForLogin(), and that resolves to the default (caching) provider, so the lookup goes back through the cached getById() at :123-142. This looks intentional rather than a defect: only IDs are cached in the list query, getById() never calls getForLogin() so there is no recursion, and the pre-existing getByOrganization() does the same at :202.
